mots.sens: This term designates the proper name of God in the Hebrew tradition, often translated as 'the LORD.' It evokes the idea of eternal existence and divine sovereignty. In the context of this psalm, it emphasizes the greatness of God, creator of the universe, and His authority over all creation, reminding believers of their dependence and reverence towards Him.

This word means 'heavens' and refers to the celestial space, often associated with the dwelling place of God. It evokes the majesty and splendor of divine creation. In this psalm, it serves to illustrate God's glory, which is manifested in the beauty and order of the heavens, reminding believers of the greatness of creation in relation to their own existence.

This term means 'praise' or 'song of praise,' and it is often used to express worship towards God. Praise is a natural response to the recognition of God's greatness. In the psalm, it highlights the importance of glorifying God for His majesty and creative work, encouraging believers to live in an attitude of gratitude and worship.

1.epoque: This psalm was composed in an ancient context, probably during the reign of David, a period marked by military struggles and deep reflections on the nature of God and humanity.
1.passage: Psalm 8 focuses on the greatness of God and the place of man in creation. It begins with a declaration of praise to God for His majesty, before exploring the dignity and responsibility of humanity as the crown of divine creation.
1.culture: In Hebrew culture, praise was essential in both communal and individual life. The psalms were sung as part of liturgy and celebrations, reinforcing the bond between the people and God.
1.interpretation: This psalm reminds us that, despite our smallness in the face of the vastness of the universe, God has given us a place of honor and responsibility. It emphasizes the dignity of humanity, created in the image of God, and our call to glorify Him through our lives.
1.commentaire: Psalm 8 invites us to contemplate the greatness of God and our place in His creation. By recognizing our dignity as beings created in His image, we are called to live in praise of our Creator. This psalm encourages us to adopt an attitude of humility and gratitude, reminding us that our existence has meaning and a mission in the divine plan.

mots.sens: This word designates God in His creative and sovereign power. It is in the plural, which can evoke the majesty and plurality of divine attributes. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes God's greatness and authority over all creation, affirming His role as Creator and supreme Lord.

The term 'name' refers to the identity and reputation of a person. In biblical culture, the name of God is synonymous with His character and attributes. In this verse, the magnificence of God's name over all the earth underscores His authority and glory, inviting believers to recognize and honor this greatness.

This word means 'height' or 'elevation,' and it evokes the idea of greatness and majesty. In the context of this verse, it indicates that God's majesty surpasses not only the earth but also the heavens, affirming His transcendent nature. This reminds us that God is above all things, and that His power is infinite.

2.epoque: Psalm 8 was written in an ancient context where Israel was seeking to understand the greatness of God in relation to His creation. This psalm is often attributed to King David, who lived about 1000 years before Christ.
2.passage: This psalm is part of a collection of praises that celebrates God's greatness and the humility of man. It is set in a context where David meditates on creation and humanity's place in the divine plan.
2.culture: In Hebrew culture, praise and worship of God were central elements of communal life. The psalms were sung during worship and celebrations, thus reinforcing collective identity and relationship with God.
2.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God's magnificence is evident throughout creation. The greatness of His name and majesty invites us to sincere worship and recognition of our place as created beings, dependent on Him.
2.commentaire: This psalm encourages us to contemplate the beauty and majesty of God in our daily lives. By recognizing the greatness of His name, we are called to live in humility and gratitude, bearing witness to His glory through our actions and words. May our lives reflect this divine magnificence, drawing others to Him.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to establish' or 'to found.' It evokes the idea of laying a solid foundation, often used in the context of creation or the establishment of a divine work. In this verse, it emphasizes that God's glory is founded on means that might be deemed weak, such as the voice of children, revealing divine wisdom in the choice of instruments to manifest His power.

This term designates 'glory' or 'splendor.' It is often associated with God's majesty and the recognition of His greatness. In the context of this verse, it highlights how God uses the most humble to reveal His glory, showing that His majesty transcends human expectations and is manifested even through the weakest.

This word means 'enemy' or 'adversary.' It is used to designate those who oppose God and His people. In this verse, it emphasizes God's ability to confound and silence those who oppose His will, reminding us that divine strength can manifest even through the weakest.

This term refers to 'nursing' or 'those who are at the breast.' It evokes the idea of dependence and vulnerability. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that even those who are most dependent and vulnerable can be powerful instruments of God's glory, showing that divine strength often manifests in human weakness.

3.epoque: This psalm is traditionally attributed to David and is set in a context where Israel faced powerful enemies, but faith in God remained central.
3.passage: Psalm 8 celebrates the greatness of God in creation while highlighting the unique place of humanity. This particular verse emphasizes how God chooses to manifest His glory through unexpected means.
3.culture: In Hebrew culture, children and vulnerable individuals were often seen as having little social value. However, this psalm reverses that perspective by affirming that God uses these voices to confound the powerful.
3.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God's strength does not reside in human power, but in His ability to use the weakest to accomplish His purposes. This teaches us that even in our vulnerability, we can be powerful witnesses of divine glory.
3.commentaire: This psalm encourages us to recognize that God often uses those whom the world despises to fulfill His plans. As believers, we must embrace our dependence on God and be open to how He can use our weaknesses for His glory. This invites us to trust God, even when we feel insignificant.

mots.sens: This word means 'heavens' and refers to the celestial expanse, the universe, often as a place of divine presence. It evokes the grandeur and majesty of God's creation, highlighting the difference between the Creator and His creation. In this verse, it reminds believers that God is sovereign over all that exists beyond our earthly understanding.

This verb means 'to form' or 'to shape', and it is often used to describe God's creative act. It implies divine intention and skill in creation, emphasizing that everything that exists has been carefully designed. In the context of this verse, it reinforces the idea that every element of the cosmos is the result of a deliberate act of God.

This term means 'star' and represents the celestial bodies that shine in the night sky. Stars are often seen as symbols of God's glory and His promises. In this verse, they serve to illustrate the magnificence of divine work and the beauty of creation, inviting wonder and worship.

This verb means 'to contemplate' or 'to look attentively'. It implies thoughtful observation and admiration of what is being observed. In the context of this verse, it suggests that the act of contemplating the heavens is not merely visual, but also spiritual, prompting reflection on God's greatness and our place in His creation.

4.epoque: Psalm 8 was written in an ancient context where creation was often perceived as a reflection of divine power, in a culture where the worship of the heavens was widespread.
4.passage: This psalm celebrates the greatness of God through the contemplation of His creation, highlighting the dignity of humanity in the divine plan. It is set in a poetic framework that invites wonder and worship.
4.culture: In Hebrew culture, the heavens and celestial bodies were often associated with the presence and glory of God, serving as a backdrop for understanding the relationship between the Creator and His creation.
4.interpretation: This verse reminds us that the contemplation of creation should lead us to recognize God's majesty. By looking at the heavens, we are invited to reflect on our place in the universe and our responsibility as beings created in the image of God.
4.commentaire: This psalm teaches us to appreciate the beauty of creation as a reflection of God's greatness. By contemplating the heavens, we are encouraged to develop an attitude of wonder and gratitude, recognizing that every star and every moon is a testament to the love and power of our Creator. This compels us to live in harmony with His will, honoring the dignity that has been conferred upon us.

mots.sens: The word 'אדם' (adam) refers to man in his essence, often interpreted as 'human being' or 'mortality'. It is derived from the root 'אדמה' (adamah), which means 'earth', thus emphasizing the connection between man and earthly creation. Theologically, this evokes the dignity of man, created in the image of God, and his unique role in the order of creation.

The term 'בּן' (ben) means 'son' and is often used to denote a relationship of filiation. In this context, it refers to humanity as children of God, emphasizing the intimacy and responsibility that comes with it. It also evokes the promise of a special relationship between God and humanity, where man is seen as an heir of divine promises.

The word 'זכר' (zakhar) means 'to remember' or 'to have in mind'. In the biblical context, this implies an active attention from God towards man, a recognition of his value and existence. It testifies to God's concern for humanity, emphasizing that God never forgets it, despite its smallness in the face of the vastness of creation.

5.epoque: This psalm was written in an ancient context where humanity was often perceived as insignificant in the face of the grandeur of divine creation.
5.passage: Psalm 8 celebrates the majesty of God in creation while highlighting the unique place of man in this order. It poses a fundamental question about the value and role of humanity in the divine plan.
5.culture: In Hebrew culture, man is seen as the pinnacle of creation, having the responsibility to dominate and care for the earth. This psalm resonates with the idea that humanity has intrinsic dignity, as a creature made in the image of God.
5.interpretation: This verse reminds us that despite our smallness and fragility, God remembers us and cares for us. It underscores God's love and grace, who chooses to interact with humanity and confer upon it immeasurable value.
5.commentaire: Psalm 8 invites us to reflect on our identity as human beings created in the image of God. By recognizing our value and role, we are called to live in communion with our Creator, to honor our responsibility towards creation, and to bear witness to God's love in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This term designates God in all His majesty and power. It evokes the idea of a sovereign creator, capable of giving life and establishing order. In this verse, it emphasizes the closeness of man to the divine, affirming that humanity is created with a dignity that reflects God's glory.

This word means 'a little less' or 'slightly inferior'. It indicates a position of proximity, highlighting that man, although created as a limited being, is nonetheless elevated above creation. This reveals the unique value of humanity in God's eyes, who confers upon it a special status.

This term translates to 'glory' and 'magnificence', and it refers to splendor and honor. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that God has endowed humanity with high dignity and responsibility, granting it a role in creation that reflects divine greatness.

This word means 'praise' or 'worship'. It evokes the idea that the creation of man is intended to glorify God. By being crowned with glory and magnificence, man is called to live in a way that honors his Creator through his actions and existence.

6.epoque: Psalm 8 was written in an ancient context, probably during the reign of David, a time when humanity faced challenges and struggles to understand its role in the universe created by God.
6.passage: This psalm celebrates the greatness of God and the unique place of man in creation. It begins with a praise to God for His majesty, then focuses on the dignity and responsibility of humanity, highlighting the contrast between divine greatness and human fragility.
6.culture: In Hebrew culture, man is seen as the image of God, which confers upon him intrinsic dignity. This view distinguishes itself from other ancient cultures that often devalued humanity in favor of the gods.
6.interpretation: This verse reminds us that, despite our smallness and fragility, we have been created with immeasurable value. God has given us a role of authority over His creation, which implies a responsibility to care for the world around us.
6.commentaire: Psalm 8 invites us to reflect on our identity as human beings created in the image of God. By recognizing our value and dignity, we are called to live in praising our Creator and acting responsibly towards His creation. This verse encourages us to embrace our role with humility and gratitude, knowing that we are crowned with glory by the One who made us.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to dominate', 'to reign', or 'to exercise authority'. It is often used in the context of sovereignty and responsibility, implying a benevolent management of creation. In this verse, it emphasizes humanity's role as stewards of God's works, which has profound implications for our responsibility towards creation.

This word means 'under' or 'beneath'. It indicates a position of submission or dependence. In this verse, it emphasizes that everything that has been created is placed under the authority of man, reinforcing the idea that humanity has a central role in the divine plan.

7.epoque: Psalm 8 was written in an ancient context where kingship and dominion over the earth were central themes, reflecting the understanding of the relationship between God, humanity, and creation.
7.passage: This psalm celebrates the greatness of God in contrast to the smallness of man, while affirming that God has conferred upon humanity a unique and exalted role in creation, highlighting the dignity and responsibility of mankind.
7.culture: In Hebrew culture, the concept of dominion involved not only power but also the responsibility to care for creation, which is a call to ethical and respectful management of the resources that God has entrusted to humanity.
7.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God has given humanity a position of authority over creation, which implies a moral and spiritual responsibility. It invites us to reflect on how we exercise this dominion as caretakers of the earth.
7.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize our role as creatures made in the image of God, called to reign with justice and love. As Christians, we must live in accordance with this responsibility, caring for our environment and acting for justice and peace in the world.

mots.sens: This word primarily refers to sheep, representing domesticated animals often used for wool, meat, and milk. In the biblical context, sheep often symbolize the people of God, highlighting the caring and protective relationship between the shepherd (God) and his sheep. The theological significance here evokes humanity's dependence on the Creator, who cares for his creatures.

This term refers to cattle, which are draft animals used for agricultural work and transport. In biblical culture, cattle symbolize strength and power, and their presence in sacrifices underscores the importance of offering to God. Spiritually, this reminds us that all strength and power must be dedicated to God.

This word means 'animal' or 'living creature', encompassing a variety of living beings in creation. It underscores the diversity of God's creation and His sovereignty over all forms of life. Theologically, this reminds us that every creature has its place and role in the divine plan.

8.epoque: Psalm 8 was written in an ancient context where agriculture and livestock were central elements of daily life and the economy of the Israelite people.
8.passage: This psalm expresses the greatness of God in contrast to the smallness of man, while affirming the dignity and role of humanity in creation. The chapter celebrates divine majesty and human responsibility towards creation.
8.culture: In Israelite culture, domesticated animals like sheep and cattle were essential for survival, serving both as economic resources and spiritual symbols in sacrifices.
8.interpretation: The verse emphasizes that all creatures, whether domesticated or wild, are under the authority of man, who is created in the image of God. This reminds us of our responsibility to care for creation while recognizing the greatness of God who has entrusted us with this task.
8.commentaire: This passage invites us to reflect on our position in creation and our responsibility towards other living beings. As beings created in the image of God, we are called to exercise our authority with wisdom and kindness, honoring the Creator through our care for His creation. This compels us to adopt an attitude of gratitude and respect towards all forms of life.

mots.sens: This term refers to birds in general, but it can also refer to anything that flies. It comes from a root that evokes the idea of rising or soaring in the air. In the context of this verse, it highlights the majesty and freedom of celestial creatures, reminding us that God is the creator of all things, including beings that inhabit the heavens.

This word means 'fish' and is used to designate aquatic creatures. Its root refers to the idea of multiplication and fertility, which is significant in the context of creation. Spiritually, this reminds us that God provides life in the seas while affirming His authority over all creation.

This term translates to 'path' or 'way', and can refer to maritime routes. It evokes the idea of direction and passage, emphasizing that even in the depths of the seas, God has established paths. This reminds us that God has a plan for every aspect of His creation, including the creatures that traverse the seas.

9.epoque: Psalm 8 was written in an ancient context, likely during the reign of David, a period when the worship of God and contemplation of His creation were central to the spiritual life of the Israelites.
9.passage: This verse is part of a psalm that celebrates the greatness of God and the importance of humanity in His creation. Chapter 8 focuses on divine majesty and human humility, highlighting the unique relationship between God and man.
9.culture: In Hebrew culture, nature was often seen as a reflection of God's glory. Birds and fish were symbols of divine providence, and their existence testified to God's creative power.
9.interpretation: This verse reminds us that all creation, from birds to fish, is under God's control. It emphasizes divine sovereignty over nature and the interconnectedness of all creatures in God's plan.
9.commentaire: Psalm 8 invites us to contemplate the majesty of God through His creation. By recognizing that God is the creator of all that lives, we are called to live with humility and gratitude. This passage encourages us to respect and care for creation while reminding us of our privileged place as human beings made in the image of God.

mots.sens: This term designates God in His majesty and creative power. It is in the plural, which may evoke the plurality of majesty and strength, while affirming the uniqueness of God. In this verse, it emphasizes God's greatness over all the earth, indicating His supreme authority over creation.

This word means 'name' and refers to someone's identity and reputation. In the biblical context, the name of God is synonymous with His character, glory, and attributes. The magnificence of God's name evokes His authority and holiness, reminding us that His name must be honored and revered.

This term refers to the earth or the world as a whole. It emphasizes the idea of the universality of God's creation. By declaring that God's name is magnificent over all the earth, the psalmist affirms that God's glory is evident in every corner of the world, calling all peoples to recognize His sovereignty.

10.epoque: This psalm was written in an ancient context, probably during the reign of David, when the recognition of God's greatness was essential for the people of Israel in the face of surrounding nations.
10.passage: Psalm 8 celebrates the majesty of God and the honor bestowed upon humanity. It begins with a praise to God, then reflects on the place of man in creation, highlighting the dignity that God has conferred upon him.
10.culture: In Hebrew culture, the name of God is of paramount importance, often associated with His presence and action in the world. The respect for God's name is an expression of faith and devotion.
10.interpretation: This verse reminds us that the magnificence of God is visible throughout creation. It invites us to contemplate the beauty and greatness of God, and to recognize His authority over our lives and the world.
10.commentaire: This psalm exhorts us to praise God for His magnificence and sovereignty. By recognizing that His name is glorious over all the earth, we are called to live as witnesses of His greatness, to honor His name in our daily lives, and to proclaim His glory around us.
